text.arabic_uthmani: ثُمَّ يُقَالُ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ

words.gloss_range: delayed sequence and ranked continuation into a later verdict beat
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) makes the saying that follows a staged next beat after the fire-contact of 83:16. The particle does more than continue the narration: it lets bodily exposure be followed by an interpretive speech-event, and the doubled mim gives the small connector an audible pause before the verdict is spoken.

topics.headline: staged sequence after fire-contact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not merely add another event; it ranks the spoken accusation as a later disclosure after the punished body has met the fire.
topics.reason: The QAC sequencer description and the 83:16 boundary context support {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) as delayed or ranked sequence into the passive saying.

topics.headline: audible weight in the connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening connector as a held beat rather than a weightless transition.
topics.reason: The doubled mim in {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) is visible in the surface and coheres with the delayed-sequence topic without creating a separate semantic branch.

words.gloss_range: passive saying as an impersonal delivered verdict introducing quoted speech
words.root_gloss_range: broad speech root including utterance, report, doctrine, negotiation, and false attribution; locally narrowed to passive delivered speech whose content carries verdict force

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: quoted demonstrative subject governed within the speech frame
closing denial verb paired with the passive saying

words.prose: {{ar:يُقَالُ}} ({{tr:yuqālu}}) opens a passive speech frame, so the speaker is not the focus and the quoted content becomes the verdict. Its imperfect form lets the saying unfold in the scene, and the following quote is treated as one delivered unit whose open cadence gives {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) room before the accusation closes. Against the deniers' dismissive speech (83:13; 83:32), the same speech field returns with changed authority; unlike direct Fire naming (52:14), this passive verdict speaks deictically, so the verdict's true naming answers the addressees' former false naming.

topics.headline: impersonal passive verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that authority rests in the delivered content, not in a named speaker or a back-and-forth dialogue.
topics.reason: The passive form of {{ar:يُقَالُ}} ({{tr:yuqālu}}) suppresses an active speaker and introduces the quote as delivered verdict rather than ordinary dialogue.

topics.headline: enacted speech content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the ayah adds a verbal act that identifies the already experienced reality, rather than leaving the punishment as mute sensation.
topics.reason: The imperfect passive and the speech-root evidence support an unfolding act of saying whose content performs the identification of {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}).

topics.headline: single quoted verdict unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks words 3-7 as one quoted accusation governed by the passive saying.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence marks the following nominal-relative sentence as the direct quoted complement of {{ar:يُقَالُ}} ({{tr:yuqālu}}).

topics.headline: recipient revealed by address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the shift from report about them to direct accusation as the quote reaches the second-person forms.
topics.reason: The passive reporting clause does not name the recipient, while the later second-person forms identify the punished group as addressees.

topics.headline: speech verdict reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a speech-field reversal: their old truth-negating speech is answered by a true verdict-speech.
topics.reason: The local pairing of {{ar:يُقَالُ}} ({{tr:yuqālu}}) with {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}) supports a contrast between authoritative saying and former falsifying.

topics.headline: contrast with other speech formulas
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that 83:17 chooses deictic verdict-speech rather than either direct Fire naming (52:14) or the deniers' own dismissive speech (83:13; 83:32).
topics.reason: The comparison survives as contrast, but it does not override the local parse of {{ar:يُقَالُ}} ({{tr:yuqālu}}) as a passive reporting verb.

topics.headline: rare passive cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that an uncommon passive shape and open cadence give the identifying quote room before the final accusation closes.
topics.reason: The contextual profile marks the exact passive-imperfect grouping as low occurrence, and the cadence row describes the local sound movement into the deictic phrase.

words.gloss_range: near demonstrative subject pointing to a displayed reality or scene

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: relative pronoun that defines the demonstrative

words.prose: {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) puts the referent in front of the quoted speech before the old denial is recalled. The demonstrative can gather the immediate fire-contact and the wider punishment scene, so the ayah points to a present, inspectable reality rather than naming only one item. Its position before {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) makes recognition precede accusation.

topics.headline: present deictic subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the denied reality placed as a present object of recognition before the accusation is explained.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) as the subject of the quoted nominal sentence.

topics.headline: composite scene reference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps both the fire-contact and the larger denied judgment-domain live, without forcing a single narrow referent too early.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the referent of {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) as ambiguous, so the composite reading survives as a controlled range rather than a resolved identification; the contrast with direct Fire naming (52:14) supports that limit.

topics.headline: identification before denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object is displayed first, then defined as the thing they used to deny.
topics.reason: The sequence {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) then {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) creates a nominal identification frame before the denial predicate lands.

topics.headline: visible and audible pointing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pointing word is not only syntactic; its written length and dhāl thread help bind the quote's movement.
topics.reason: The written surface of {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) and its sound relation to the following relative and final verb are visible local features.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun linking the displayed referent to the defining denial clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: demonstrative antecedent defined by the relative clause
final verb completing the relative clause

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) turns the pointed {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) into a referent defined by the addressees' own denial. Its masculine singular agreement binds the following clause to the displayed referent, while the relative construction keeps the referent broad enough to include the fire, judgment, and the truth-claim now made present. Because the completing verb waits until the end, the quote carries the listener from recognition into the final accusation.

topics.headline: relative definition by denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the present reality is identified through the addressees' repeated action toward it, not by a simple noun label.
topics.reason: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) is the relative predicate after {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}), and its following clause is syntactically forced.

topics.headline: open composite relative scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can keep a composite denied reality in view without treating the pronoun as a license for uncontrolled referent expansion.
topics.reason: The relative can gather a matter, event, or proposition, but local agreement and the resumptive chain keep the scope tied to {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}).

topics.headline: linked and delayed closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and follows the relative link as it carries the accusation forward until the closing verb completes it.
topics.reason: The joined relative surface and dhāl echo are local features, and the relative clause remains incomplete until {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}).

words.gloss_range: second-person plural past auxiliary making the denial a former habitual state
words.root_gloss_range: broad being, occurrence, place, suretyship, and condition range; locally narrowed to past auxiliary statehood with an imperfect predicate

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: imperfect predicate governed by the past auxiliary

words.prose: {{ar:كُنتُم}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) changes the charge from a single past act into a former inhabited pattern: they used to be in the state of falsifying. Its second-person plural ending makes the punished group hear the verdict as direct address, and its auxiliary role keeps the lexical action waiting until {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}). Same-surah and cross-surah echoes sharpen that movement: reported conduct becomes accusation, while the habitual-denial frame is specialized here as direct confrontation (74:46; 83:29).

topics.headline: direct second-person address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deniers can no longer remain third-person examples; the verdict addresses them as you.
topics.reason: The second masculine plural ending in {{ar:كُنتُم}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) agrees with the closing verb and fixes the addressees inside the quote.

topics.headline: habitual past denial state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that denial is charged as a sustained past condition, not as one isolated denial.
topics.reason: {{ar:كُنتُم}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) is a perfect auxiliary governing an imperfect predicate, so the local construction selects habitual past statehood.

topics.headline: being family state coloring
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the past denial as a formed condition or mode of being, while the grammar keeps auxiliary past state as the selected local function.
topics.reason: The broader {{ar:ك و ن}} ({{tr:k-w-n}}) family supports state and condition coloring, but local grammar prevents place, suretyship, or independent becoming senses from governing {{ar:كُنتُم}} ({{tr:kuntum}}).

topics.headline: syntax delays the denial verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the accusation stretched across the relative clause before the denial verb lands.
topics.reason: {{ar:كُنتُم}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) opens the internal clause, while the prepositional object-domain and final predicate delay completion.

topics.headline: habit-frame echoes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this direct accusation as part of a wider habitual-action frame, with 74:46 as confession contrast and 83:29 as same-surah habit parallel.
topics.reason: The echo rows support formulaic and same-surah comparison, but the local clause remains a direct second-person accusation rather than a confession or the mockery scene of 83:29.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus third masculine singular suffix marking the denial's object-domain

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: displayed referent resumed by the attached pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) keeps the disputed object grammatically attached to the act of falsifying. The bā frames denial as concerning or in relation to the displayed referent, while the attached pronoun resumes {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) without repeating a noun. Because it appears before the final verb, the old object-domain is placed in view before the accusation closes; the earlier denial of the Day (83:11) is now compressed into the shown it.

topics.headline: bā object-domain relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices denial framed as relation to a displayed domain, not as a bare unattached object rejection.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) as the prepositional complement governed by {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}).

topics.headline: resumptive pronoun chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one referent carried from displayed this to compact it inside the relative clause.
topics.reason: The suffix in {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) is marked as a resumptive pronoun tied to the displayed referent, while the masculine singular form packages the referent as one grammatical object-domain.

topics.headline: preposed object before denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the disputed it placed before the final verb, so the referent frames the accusation before it lands.
topics.reason: The word order puts {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) between {{ar:كُنتُم}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) and {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}).

topics.headline: Day-denial compressed to it
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the named denial of the Day (83:11) become a compact pronoun attached to the reality now displayed.
topics.reason: The same-surah echo is lexical and referentially plausible, while local grammar keeps {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) as the resumptive complement inside the relative clause.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural imperfect Form II falsifying or declaring false, governed by the past auxiliary and linked to a bā object-domain
words.root_gloss_range: broad falsehood family including lying, declaring false, failed expectation, urging formulas, and deceptive appearance; locally narrowed to Form II active false-classifying of the displayed referent

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: past auxiliary that frames the denial as habitual
bā-governed object-domain attached to the denial verb

words.prose: {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}) closes the ayah with the action that defined the addressees: active false-classifying of the reality now displayed. The Form II shape selects declaring something false rather than simply lying, and its imperfect predicate under {{ar:كُنتُم}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) makes that falsifying a repeated past practice. Because the verb is tied to {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}), the charge is denial concerning this shown referent; because it is the final word, the verdict lands on the old falsification itself. The opening true saying and the closing denial verb answer each other, turning the surah's earlier denier-language into direct address (83:10-12; 83:11; 74:46).

topics.headline: bā-governed falsifying
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verb is syntactically attached to the displayed it, so denial remains directed concerning a referent.
topics.reason: The verb instance records {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}) with a bā complement, and attachment evidence assigns {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) as that complement.

topics.headline: Form II declaring false
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the accusation is active false-classification of truth, not merely the act of telling lies.
topics.reason: The local derived form and V4 declaring-false branch support {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}) as false-classifying rather than simple lying or reciprocal disputation.

topics.headline: falsehood family pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the broader falsehood field pressing against the deniers, while the local form keeps the selected sense as declaring the truth false.
topics.reason: The broader {{ar:ك ذ ب}} ({{tr:k-dh-b}}) family provides falsehood and posture coloring, but the local surface is {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}), not a separate Form V verb.

topics.headline: habitual addressed agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verb keeps their agency and repeated practice audible inside the past-state frame.
topics.reason: {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}) agrees with {{ar:كُنتُم}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) and remains an imperfect predicate within the past auxiliary construction.

topics.headline: verdict speech reversal and echoes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the surah's denier-language culminate as direct accusation, while the verdict's saying answers their former falsifying (83:10-12; 83:11; 74:46).
topics.reason: The same-surah rows tie {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}) to denier language in 83:10-12 and 83:11, while the q-w-l pairing supports the answer between true saying and false-classifying.

topics.headline: relative-clause final closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the relative clause and the whole ayah wait for this last verb to disclose the charge.
topics.reason: The relative clause opened by {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) is completed by {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}), which also occupies final position.

topics.headline: tightened dhāl closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final accusation tighten around the doubled dhāl, matching the force of repeated falsifying.
topics.reason: The shaddah in {{ar:تُكَذِّبُونَ}} ({{tr:tukadhdhibūna}}) is a visible local sound feature and coheres with the closing accusation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Denied report becomes a present demonstrable object.** `ق و ل` B001 supplies uttered speech, `ك ذ ب` B002 supplies declaring something false, and `ك و ن` B001 supplies being or occurrence. Structurally, the passive `يُقَالُ` frames a demonstrative `هَٰذَا`, shifting the denied matter from prior discourse to present encounter. I assign speech the role of identifying and the demonstrative the role of evidential pointing. The abductive move is that occurrence itself now disproves denial. The ayah reads as verification by presence.

2. **Their former attribution of falsehood is returned as a verdict on them.** `ق و ل` B005 supplies false saying or attribution, while `ك ذ ب` B001 supplies falsehood in speech or action. The same speech-domain they used in 83:13 is now used over them in the passive. I infer a role reversal: the authority to classify reality has moved from their dismissive saying to the event's own indication. The ayah reads as a reversal of who gets to name what is false.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The reversed public laughter of 83:34 and the final interrogative of 83:36 showed that the spoken identification here begins a larger reversal of verdict-making, not only a private confrontation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The consequence itself becomes a saying.** Lexical evidence: ق و ل/B014, "thing's saying as indication," in يُقَالُ, alongside the ordinary B001 "uttered speech." Structural cue: the deictic هَٰذَا follows direct fire exposure at 83:16 and precedes the contrasting book and bliss at 83:18-22. Assigned role: B001 supplies the pronouncement; B014 makes the indicated condition carry its own evidentiary speech. Abductive move: I infer that هَٰذَا points to the experienced reality as proof, not merely to a verbal proposition. Reading change: the utterance does more than name punishment; it lets what is present answer the former denial.

2. **The failed charge is identified in public.** Lexical evidence: ك ذ ب/B004, "fulfilling or failing a charge," in تُكَذِّبُونَ. Structural cue: 83:13 records their counter-charge that the signs are old tales; 83:16 realizes what they denied; 83:18-21 supplies another marked record and its witnesses. Assigned role: B004 turns their prior declaration into the proposition now shown to have failed. Abductive move: I infer a public evidentiary reversal from passive speech, deixis, record, and witness. Reading change: هَٰذَا identifies not only the denied object but the collapse of the deniers' own claim.

3. **Habit is carried intact into recognition.** Lexical evidence: ك و ن/B001, "being, occurrence, or temporal predication," in كُنتُم, and ك ذ ب/B002 in تُكَذِّبُونَ. Structural cue: the past auxiliary plus imperfect recalls the recurring إِذَا-response at 83:13; the deictic present now confronts that duration. Assigned role: ك و ن/B001 preserves the prior state as a temporally extended identity that can be matched to its present object. Abductive move: I infer that the pronouncement performs record-like temporal matching between repeated act and realized outcome. Reading change: the clause is not a generic reminder; it binds a durable practice of denial to the immediately present "this."

4. **Authoritative speech reverses false attribution.** Lexical evidence: ق و ل/B005, "false saying or false attribution," activated by contrast within يُقَالُ. Structural cue: the denier's قَالَ at 83:13 falsely classified signs; here the passive يُقَالُ follows realized consequence. Assigned role: B005 characterizes the earlier speech that the present saying corrects. Abductive move: I infer a deliberate speech-for-speech reversal from the repeated root and opposed contexts. Reading change: the passive pronouncement becomes a correction of naming authority: their saying no longer controls what the indicated reality is called.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 83:18-22 showed that authoritative "saying" is answered not only by another proposition but by register, witness, enrollment, and lived allocation. That later embodiment confirmed ق و ل/B014: the indicated reality speaks through what it makes publicly present.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sayı, miktar ya da ölçü bakımından çok olmayışını bildirir. Bundan yoksulluk ve düşüklük, bir şeyi az sayma veya az gösterme ve belirli yapılarda hiçlik ya da seyrek gerçekleşme anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

root_profile.summary: Kökün anlam ağı, söz ve davranışta doğruluğa aykırılık ile başkasını yalan sayma çekirdeğinden; yükümlülük, savaş hamlesi, gecikmeme, süt kesilmesi, hayvan hareketi, iç benlik ve kumaş görünüşü gibi sözlüksel olarak özelleşmiş alanlara uzanır.
